The Tourist Development Council (TDC), at the regular meeting on August 7, 2025, recommended reimbursing Citrus Golf Trail for the 2025 Citrus Golf Trail Ladies Invitational golf tournament held at Sun 'N Lake Golf Club on December 27- 31, 2025.
The TDC recommends reimbursing up to a total of $15,000.00 for the event, requiring evidence of up to 750 room nights generated by the event, being reimbursed at $20/per room night. This grant will be to cover eligible costs associated with facility rental and approved reimbursable items under the Sport Event Grant guidelines for the 2025 Citrus Golf Trail Ladies Invitational.
The event received a Sport Event Tourist Development Grant for 2024 in the amount of $15,000 that required room night verifications for the entire amount at $20/room night. The event generated 300 verified room nights, and so received $6,000 reimbursement.
The event received a 2-year New Event Tourist Development Grant for 2022 and 2023 in the amount of $12,000 with room verifications required for up to $6,000. The event was able to show 315 verified room nights in 2023 and 344 in 2022, and so received the full $12,000 funding each year.

At its October 30, 2025 meeting, the Tourist Development Council (TDC) voted to recommend Board approval of a new Facility Rental Fee Grant Funding Program policy as part of the TDC’s updated grant framework.
The Facility Rental Fee Grant Funding Program provides limited funding (up to $5,000 per event) for eligible tourism-driving events held at County-managed facilities. The program offsets approved facility rental fees for multi-day events that attract a significant percentage of participants from outside Highlands County, thereby stimulating local lodging demand and visitor spending. category: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting
description:
This position is critical in maintaining the County’s ability to provide timely building inspections and plan review services to residents, contractors, and developers in accordance with the Florida Building Code and National Electrical Code.
Highlands County is experiencing sustained and measurable growth, and the Building Department must expand to ensure safe, compliant construction and maintain service levels expected by our community. The addition of this inspector is essential for the continued effective operation of the department.
Highlands County has seen an increase in development activity, with new housing starts rising by 15.53% in the past year. This growth directly drives inspection volume, placing increased pressure on our limited inspection staff and challenging our goal of providing next-day inspections.
Key impacts of this request include:
Maintaining Public Safety and Code Compliance. Delays in inspections can lead to safety risks for the public.
Preserving Next-Day Inspection Service. Current staffing levels are at capacity. Without additional support, maintaining next-day service will become increasingly difficult.
Supporting Economic Development. Timely inspections are essential for keeping residential and commercial projects on schedule.
The success of this position will be evaluated using the following performance measures:
Sustained Next-Day Inspection Availability. Maintain or improve our current turnaround time for inspection requests.
Inspection Quality and Compliance. Ensure all inspections meet state and local regulatory requirements with accuracy and professionalism.
Customer Service Satisfaction. Continuing to provide dependable support to contractors and residents, reflected through reduced delays and positive feedback.

Highlands County has negotiated a Real Property Purchase Agreement with Center Ridge Caretaking, Inc. and Marion E. Stephens IV for the acquisition of property adjacent to the Highlands County Multi-Sport Complex. The intent of this purchase of 43.87 acres is to support the long-term expansion of the Multi-Sport Complex to accommodate future sports tourism growth, expand programming for tourists and local residents, and enhance regional recreation opportunities.
The total purchase price of $724,000 plus an estimated $20,000 in acquisition costs will be funded through the Tourist Development Trust Fund (Cost Center 5309/3rd Penny), as the acquisition directly advances tourism development objectives and is authorized under Florida Statute 125.0104. with a potential of $100,000 originating from General Revenue pending a future budget amendment.
To offset a portion of the acquisition cost, the County has been approved by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) for a reimbursable Florida Communities Trust (FCT) grant award in the amount of $372,000. The formal FCT Grant Agreement is forthcoming from the Florida DEP. Once received, it will be brought before the Board for review and approval.
Approval of the Real Property Purchase Agreement at this time will allow the County to move forward with securing the property necessary for the planned Multi-Sport Complex expansion while positioning the County to request reimbursement back to the TDC’s 5309 Cost Center upon execution of the state grant.

description:
Highlands County Fire Rescue recently received a cash donation totaling $42,125.08 from the Estate of Mr. Scott DeRoller, which provided for the purchase of two (2) Lucas Chest Compression Systems. These life-saving devices deliver high-quality, consistent cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in accordance with American Heart Association (AHA) standards, significantly improving patient outcomes during cardiac arrest emergencies.
The Board’s formal recognition of this donation acknowledges the generosity and community spirit of Mr. DeRoller, whose contribution directly enhances Highlands County Fire Rescue’s ability to deliver exceptional emergency medical care. This act of generosity reflects the strong partnership between Highlands County residents and their public safety agencies, exemplifying a shared commitment to protecting and preserving life throughout the community.

category: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting
description:
GIS stands for Geographic Information Science and is a way for us to manage and analyze information, or data, about our world that has a location attached to it. We can then present that data to our audience, or users, in the form of maps, applications and other tools. The County has implemented GIS across nearly all departments and staff continue to provide geographic data and information to residents in new and engaging ways.
GIS Day is an international event that demonstrates how geography and real-world applications of GIS are making differences in business, government and society. These events are a way to celebrate the impactful work of dedicated GIS professionals and serve to ignite the imagination and ambition of future innovators who will further advance global progress using GIS.

attachments.name: Agenda Packet - Resolution 25-26-010  NO Large Vehicles. BURKETT.FINAL.SGS 11.18.2025

category: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting
description:
Burkett Avenue is a County owned roadway which is considered a rural major collector road that is designed to provide direct access to area properties, to connect local traffic to arterial roads, and to facilitate local traffic flow but is not designed for high traffic volume or impacts like arterial roadways. Large vehicles utilizing this roadway are causing damage and destruction to the roadway. The County has determined that it is in the best interests of and will protect the health, safety, and welfare of the traveling public to restrict access of large vehicle traffic on Burkett Avenue.
The “No Through Trucks” traffic signs will be placed in the FDOT Right-of-way on SR 66 by FDOT at their expense. FDOT will determine the exact location.
One “No Through Trucks” traffic sign will be placed in the County Right-of-way on Woodbury Avenue from Lakewood Road. One “No Through Trucks” traffic sign will be placed in the County Right-of-way on Burkette Ave from SR 66. Signs within the County Right-of-way will be placed by the County Traffic Operations.
meeting: Regular Board of County Commissioners Meeting
title: Request Adoption of Resolution No. 25-26-010 Restricting Large Vehicle Traffic on Burkett Avenue.

At its October 30, 2025 meeting, the Tourist Development Council (TDC) approved the attached policies for its grant funding programs. The updated policy framework includes revisions to existing grant categories and introduces two new programs designed to further the County’s strategic tourism development goals.
The existing High Impact Signature Event, New Event, and Sports & Special Event grant categories have been updated to clarify eligibility criteria, strengthen accountability, and ensure consistency with the TDC’s long-term tourism objectives.
Two new categories are being proposed for addition:Tourism Marketing Assistance Program (TMAP): Designed to assist Highlands County tourism-related businesses—such as attractions, outfitters, and cultural or heritage sites—in developing out-of-county marketing initiatives and tourism-focused promotional efforts that attract visitors and encourage extended stays during non-peak months (April–December). The reimbursable program supports digital and e-marketing campaigns, website enhancements, and other eligible activities that strengthen the Visit Sebring brand and drive visitation to Highlands County.
Facility Rental Fee Grant Funding Program: Provides limited funding (up to $5,000 per event) for eligible tourism-driving events held at County-managed facilities. The program offsets approved facility rental fees for multi-day events that attract a significant percentage of participants from outside Highlands County, thereby stimulating local lodging demand and visitor spending.
Upon Board approval, the updated policies will take effect immediately and apply to all new grant applications considered at the January 2026 TDC meeting and thereafter.

category: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting
description:
We are currently requesting approval of Resolution 25.26.009 for the three (3) year Local Housing Assistance Plan (LHAP) covering fiscal years 2025-2026, 2026-2027, and 2027-2028.
In 1992, the State Legislature passed the Sadowski Affordable Housing Act. This affordable housing program is funded through documentary tax stamps on deeds recorded in Florida. The State Housing Initiatives Partnership (SHIP) Program provides services that develop and improve the economic condition of the community. Every three (3) years, Highlands County is required to submit a new three (3) year local housing assistance plan to the Florida Housing Finance Corporation.
The local housing assistance plans are intended to increase the availability of affordable residential units by combining local resources and cost-saving measures into a local housing partnership and using private and public funds to reduce the cost of housing.
According to Florida Statute, Chapter 420.9075, local housing assistance plans are to be created to make affordable residential units available to persons of very low income, low income, or moderate income and to persons who have special housing needs, including, but not limited to, homeless people, the elderly, migrant farmworkers, and persons with disabilities. Each local government must use a minimum of 20 percent (20%) of its local housing distribution to serve persons with special needs as defined in statute 420.0004.
Two constraints are placed on the use of these funds. The first constraint requires at least sixty-five percent (65%) of the funds to be used for home ownership activities, and seventy-five percent (75%) of the funds used for construction, rehabilitation, or emergency repair of affordable, eligible housing.
The second constraint requires all units constructed, rehabilitated or otherwise provided funding assistance through the State Housing Initiatives Partnership (SHIP) program to be occupied as follows: At least thirty percent (30%) of the units must be occupied by very-low income persons and an additional thirty percent (30%) by low-income persons. The remainder may be occupied by eligible persons including moderate-income persons.
Additionally, not more than 20 percent (20%) of the funds made available in each county and eligible municipality from the local housing distribution may be used for manufactured housing.
The required provisions and constraints of the Florida Statutes have been incorporated into the content of the SHIP LHAP. The incentive Strategies detail the policies and procedures for the adopted incentives. The Exhibits include the Administrative Budget, Timeline for Encumbrance and Expenditures, Housing Delivery Goals Chart, LHAP Certification, and the associated Resolution.

category: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting
description:
In 1992, the State Legislature passed the Sadowski Affordable Housing Act. This affordable housing program is funded through documentary tax stamps on deeds recorded in Florida. The State Housing Initiatives Partnership (SHIP) Program provides services that develops and improves the economic condition of the community. Every three (3) years, Highlands County is required to submit a new three (3) year local housing assistance plan to the Florida Housing Finance Corporation. We are currently requesting approval for the three (3) year plan covering fiscal years 2025-2026, 2026-2027, and 2027-2028 with associated Resolution 25.29.009.
The local housing assistance plans are intended to increase the availability of affordable residential units by combining local resources and cost-saving measures into a local housing partnership and using private and public funds to reduce the cost of housing.
According to Florida Statute, Chapter 420.9075, local housing assistance plans are to be created to make affordable residential units available to persons of very low income, low income, or moderate income and to persons who have special housing needs, including, but not limited to, homeless people, the elderly, migrant farmworkers, and persons with disabilities. Each local government must use a minimum of 20 percent (20%) of its local housing distribution to serve persons with special needs as defined in statute 420.0004.
Two constraints are placed on the use of these funds. The first constraint requires at least sixty-five percent (65%) of the funds to be used for home ownership activities, and seventy-five percent (75%) of the funds used for construction, rehabilitation, or emergency repair of affordable, eligible housing.
The second constraint requires all units constructed, rehabilitated or otherwise provided funding assistance through the State Housing Initiatives Partnership (SHIP) program to be occupied as follows: At least thirty percent (30%) of the units must be occupied by very-low income persons and an additional thirty percent (30%) by low-income persons. The remainder may be occupied by eligible persons including moderate-income persons.
Additionally, not more than 20 percent (20%) of the funds made available in each county and eligible municipality from the local housing distribution may be used for manufactured housing.
The required provisions and constraints of the Florida Statutes have been incorporated into the content of the SHIP LHAP. The incentive Strategies detail the policies and procedures for the adopted incentives. The Exhibits include the Administrative Budget, Timeline for Encumbrance and Expenditures, Housing Delivery Goals Chart, LHAP Certification, and the associated Resolution.
meeting: Regular Board of County Commissioners Meeting
title: Public hearing to request adoption of Resolution 25-29-009 for the 2025-2026, 2026-2027, and 2027-2028 Local Housing Assistance Plan.

description:
Currently our Code of Ordinances does not regulate boarding operations and facilities for dog or cat daycares in Highlands County, because of this those businesses are not consistently keeping records of vaccinations or registrations on hand for dogs or cats while in their boarding facilities. This recordkeeping should be required for the boarder operations or facilities to have on site while the animals are in their care.
Such an ordinance would propose a boarder operation, facility or daycare for dogs or cats to be required to keep records of vaccination and registration on hand for the animals in their care, the language for this ordinance can be included with the Hobby Breeder ordinance and adopted at the same time. If approved this ordinance would be enforced through a formal complaint process to the Highlands County Animal Services Department and would be enforced with the civil citation process Chapter 2, Article XII, Section 4. A violation of this section constitutes a Class I violation.
Chapter 4, Article I, Section 4.5-2 Vaccination required is currently adopted; All dogs, cats, and ferrets four months of age or older must be vaccinated by a licensed veterinarian against rabies with a vaccine that is licensed by the United States Department of Agriculture for use in those species.
Chapter 4, Article I, Section 4.5-3 Animals to be registered is currently adopted; The owner of each dog, cat or ferret vaccinated pursuant to Section 4.5-2 of this article is required to register the vaccinated animal with Highlands County Animal Control within 30 days after the animal is vaccinated and pay the registration fee.
meeting: Regular Board of County Commissioners Meeting

category: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting
description:
Section 8.5-24(c) of the Highlands County Code sets forth standards governing the transportation of municipal solid waste, construction and demolition waste, and horticultural trash in unenclosed vehicles, including the requirement that such loads be fully and properly tarped.Currently, the Code imposes a specific surcharge—an additional tipping fee of $50.00 per ton—for any person transporting an un-tarped load in violation of the ordinance. This static fee structure limits the County’s ability to adjust penalties in response to evolving operational costs, policy needs, or budget priorities.
This ordinance amends Sec. 8.5-24 to update the language to allow for code enforcement citations to be issued associated with un-tarped loads.

description:
The Special Event Permit Ordinance was adopted on March 16, 2021, to promote the success of Special Events, manage the impacts of Special Events, and protect the public health, safety and welfare at Special Events. Since the adoption of the ordinance, staff has determined that subsequent clarification is needed in reference to the application requirements. Section 8.7-6(b) of the County Code, states: "If the special events administrator determines that an applicant otherwise meets the criteria for a special event permit, but additional information is needed, the applicant shall submit such additional information in the form requested before a permit decision will be made." Staff is proposing to add clarification to this Section, that the additional information that is requested can include, but is not limited to, proof of insurance for the protection of the public, emergency access routes, and proof of required specialty licensing.
The purpose of this Statement of Legislative Intent is to receive direction from the Board.
meeting: First Monthly Board Meeting
title: Consider Statement of Legislative Intent for an amendment to the Special Event Permit Ordinance for subsequent clarification.

category: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting
description:
On August 21, 2025, the Health Insurance Committee approved changes to the medical plan structure, reducing 3 medical plan offerings down to 2. The 2 proposed medical plan options for year 2026 are the Base Plan HDHP (high deductible health plan) and the Buy up-Plan. The base plan would remain free to the employee. Additional benefits include 2 dental plans, vision, basic life, voluntary life, AD & D, short-term and long-term disability, and the employee assistance program. The Base Plan HDHP benefits will remain the same as the current plan. Currently, there are 831 employees and 512 spouses/dependents for a total of 1,343 members.
The summary of plan changes is as follows:
Buy-up Plan
a. Increase in network single deductible from $1,500 to $2,000
b. Increase in network OOP Single from $4,500 to $5,000 and Family from $9,000 to $10,000
c. Increase in network PCP from $30 to $60
d. Increase in network specialist from $55 to $75.
e. Adding a RX Deductible of $500
ASO
Increase to the composite rate from $43 to $43.86.
Specific Stop Loss
Increase the Spec Deductible from $225K to $250K
Composite rate changes from $115.01 to $112.72.
Aggregate Stop Loss
Increase to the composite rate from $6.51 to $6.55.
Medicare Advantage
Rate increases from $355.60 to $398.27.
Employee assistance program
Rate increases from $1.28 to $1.41.

description: Highlands County currently operates seven WeatherSTEM stations across the county. The County asked for additional stations through this agreement with the Florida Division of Emergency Management (FDEM), and FDEM approved one. The new station will be installed at the Highlands County Landfill. WeatherSTEM stations send real-time weather data to Highlands County Emergency Management, the National Weather Service, and FDEM. Partner agencies and Highlands County residents can also see the data, which helps the whole community stay prepared.

category: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting
description:
Chapter 12, Article 16, Building Code, Division 4, Contractors and Builder-Owners, of the Highlands County Code of Ordinances currently establishes local licensing requirements for certain Specialty Contractors and Handypersons.
Recent changes to Chapter 489, Florida Statutes, have limited the County's authority to license Specialty Contractors and Handypersons occupations. Section 489.113(6)(a)6, Florida Statutes, governs certain Specialty Contractor licensing classifications, as designated by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board. Section 489.117(4)(a)1., Florida Statutes, prohibits local governments from licensing Handypersons, while Section 489.117(4)(a)3. preserves local licensing authority for Fence Contractors and Soffit, Siding, Fascia, and Gutter Contractors.
Accordingly, amendments to the Highlands County Code of Ordinances are mandated to ensure consistency with Florida law, and maintain the legal enforceability of licensing requirements administered by the Highlands County Building Division.
meeting: Regular Board of County Commissioners Meeting

description:
The property adjacent to the Government Center parking area and across the street from the main Facilities Maintenance building was evaluated by Business Services and County Administration. Due to its proximity and strategic location, the property was determined to be a beneficial acquisition for future County expansion.
Business Services issued a Letter of Interest to Sebring Ventures, LLC on July 17, 2026, as a preliminary inquiry into a potential acquisition. Multiple independent appraisals were conducted on the four parcels, and on October 7, 2026, the property owners accepted Highlands County's final negotiated purchase offer of $425,000.00.
Following successful negotiations, the County Administrator and Sebring Ventures, LLC executed a Letter of Intent (LOI) to purchase the properties on October 20, 2026, contingent upon a mutually agreed Real Property Purchase Agreement approved by the Highlands County Board of County Commissioners. The signed agreement is attached for your consideration and approval.
The properties being considered are located at 643 S. Fernleaf Ave., 651 S. Fernleaf Ave., 663 S. Fernleaf Ave., and 710 S. Commerce Ave.

The regular Board meetings are held on the first and third Tuesday of every month at 9:00 a.m., followed on those dates by the meetings of the Special Districts at 9:30 a.m., or as soon thereafter as possible. However, if a nationally recognized holiday falls on a Monday, that week's meeting will be moved to Thursday (pursuant to Resolution 22-23-18). In 2027, there are four (4) meetings impacted by this exception:
Martin Luther King Jr. Day holiday (Monday, January 18, 2027). That meeting will take place on Thursday, January 21, 2027.
Memorial Day holiday (Monday, May 31, 2027). That meeting will take place on Thursday, June 3, 2027.
Fourth of July holiday (Monday, July 5, 2027). That meeting will take place on Thursday, July 8, 2027.
Labor Day holiday (Monday, September 6, 2027). That meeting will take place on Thursday, September 9, 2027.
